damascus.text: At the end of 2025, 3.7 million Syrian refugees lived in the countries next to Syria, and 5.5 million people were displaced inside Syria. After Assad fell on 8 December 2024, about 1.3 million refugees went home in 2025, about three times more than in 2024. UNHCR warns that this does not mean Syria is safe.

lampedusa.text: On 3 October 2013, 368 people died in one shipwreck off Lampedusa. Since 2014, 26,865 people have died or gone missing between North Africa and Italy. The worst year was 2016, with 4,574.

rome.text: In 2016, 181,436 people reached Italy by sea, a record and 18% more than in 2015.
rome.source: UNHCR, Italian Ministry of the Interior

budapest.text: In early September 2015, thousands of people were stuck at Budapest’s Keleti station. On the night of 4 to 5 September, Austria and Germany let them in. On 15 September, Hungary finished its 175 km fence on the border with Serbia.

prag.text: Czechia hosts more Ukrainian refugees per person than any other EU country: 36 per 1,000 people, 393,055 people at the end of 2025. The EU average is 9.7.

warsaw.text: Poland hosts about 969,000 Ukrainians under temporary protection, the second most in the EU. At the border with Belarus, 132 people have died or gone missing, 44 of them on the Polish side.

project.heading: The Project
project.body1: IOM's Missing Migrants Project tracks deaths of migrants, including refugees and asylum-seekers, who have gone missing along mixed migration routes worldwide. The research behind this project began with the October 2013 tragedies, when at least 368 individuals died in two shipwrecks near the Italian island of Lampedusa. Since then, Missing Migrants Project has developed into an important hub and advocacy source of information that media, researchers, and the general public access for the latest information.
project.body2: With a count surpassing 30,000 lives lost during migration since 2014, IOM calls on all the world's governments to address what it describes as "an epidemic of crime and abuse."
